artworks.title: Death of Pentheus (Attic red-figure kylix)
artworks.description: On this Louvre cup maenads tear Pentheus apart — Agave among the Theban women who, in Euripides, mistake her son for a lion on Cithaeron and bring his head home in triumph.

artworks.title: The Torment of Pentheus (House of the Vettii, Pompeii)
artworks.description: A Pompeian fresco restages the sparagmos: Pentheus torn by bacchants — the scene whose climax, in the Bacchae, is Agave waking to her son's head in her hands.

artworks.title: The Death of Pentheus (from Ovid's Metamorphoses)
artworks.description: A Metropolitan Museum plate after Ovid titles the horror plainly: Pentheus torn by his mother and sisters — Agave's madness as a set-piece of the Metamorphoses cycle.

popCulture.title: The Bacchae
popCulture.creator: Euripides
popCulture.description: Euripides' last tragedy makes Agave its most terrible recognition: the Cadmeid princess, mad on Cithaeron, returns carrying Pentheus' head and only then sees what Dionysus has done.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid retells the Theban sparagmos with Agave first among the maenads — the mother who begins the tearing and ends in exile.

popCulture.title: Agave (daughter of Cadmus)
popCulture.description: Daughter of Cadmus and Harmonia, mother of Pentheus — the princess Dionysus drove to kill her own son on Cithaeron.
